storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the abstract axis physical: notes in hand versus people beside him.
storyboard.claim: The first axis is focus: task-oriented versus people-oriented.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding work notes, turned toward a colleague: the task in his hand versus the person beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the grid setup from the axes introduction.

storyboard.addedInformation: The walking body shows pace, which the words alone cannot show muted.
storyboard.claim: The second axis is energy: reserved and slow versus outgoing and fast.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman striding briskly across the office: pace made visible in his walk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the second axis after the task-versus-people axis.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names the product of crossing the lines: four quadrants, not two lines.
storyboard.claim: Crossing focus and energy creates four behavioral quadrants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Four-Color Grid with its crossing axes, Erikson pointing to the four quadrants.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Crosses the two axes just established into one grid.

storyboard.addedInformation: Lays out the four named buckets the narration only lists in speech.
storyboard.claim: The four quadrants are four languages: red, yellow, green, blue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A four-bucket sorter: Red, Yellow, Green, Blue side by side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sorts the new grid into its four named colors.

storyboard.addedInformation: The host's open gesture concedes the limit before defending the tool.
storyboard.claim: Nobody fits neatly into one box; nobody is a monolith.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson speaking plainly to camera, hands open: no grid on screen, just the caveat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pushes back on the neat boxes just drawn.

storyboard.addedInformation: The notes in hand carry the statistics the voice cites.
storyboard.claim: About 80% blend two dominant colors; only 5% are purely one color.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson holding his notes with the figures: most people blend two colors.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quantifies the nobody-is-one-color caveat with statistics.

storyboard.addedInformation: The thinking pose shows the inner complexity the grid risks flattening.
storyboard.claim: You are a complex recipe, not a single ingredient.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman paused in thought, hand to chin: a whole person, not one ingredient.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the statistic into a personal warning against dismissing the grid.

storyboard.addedInformation: The worried thinker carries the psychologists' objection without staging trauma.
storyboard.claim: Psychologists object the grid flattens trauma and neuroplasticity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson thinking hard, brow furrowed: weighing the critique about the soul's complexity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Voices the expert critique of the parlor-trick grid.

storyboard.addedInformation: Bare staging keeps the charge verbal: no color icon to confuse with endorsement.
storyboard.claim: Reducing shifting identities to one color is dangerously reductive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson thinking, no grid icon beside him: the reductive label is the subject.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sharpens the critique to its verdict on single-color labels.

storyboard.addedInformation: The home room places the kids-versus-boss split the narration names.
storyboard.claim: You act differently with your kids than with your boss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman at home, thinking it over: the kids context versus the boss context.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the reductiveness personal with kids-versus-boss.

storyboard.addedInformation: The chains make the felt cage literal: bound by a permanent label.
storyboard.claim: A permanent label feels like a psychological cage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bound chains beside a slumped Everyman: the label as imprisonment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the discomfort into the cage metaphor.

storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing gesture sells the hammer as demolition, not a held object.
storyboard.claim: A 30 lb sledgehammer is perfect for demolishing a concrete wall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson pointing forcefully, as if indicating a concrete wall to demolish.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the cage fear with the sledgehammer analogy.

storyboard.addedInformation: The small framed photo is the delicate task the hammer would smash.
storyboard.claim: That hammer destroys the house on a delicate picture frame.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried Everyman carefully holding a small framed photo in the living room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Flips the hammer from right tool to wrong one.

storyboard.addedInformation: The struck cage rejects the cage reading while the grid stays as a tool.
storyboard.claim: The grid is not a cage; it is a blunt tool for mental shortcuts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Four-Color Grid beside Erikson, with the cage label struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the analogy: the grid is the hammer, not the cage.

storyboard.addedInformation: The pressured thinker shows the default tool surfacing under strain.
storyboard.claim: The grid reveals which tool you default to, especially under pressure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The grid in front of the worker under pressure: the default tool each colour reaches for when it is stressed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States what the tool is for: defaults under pressure.

storyboard.addedInformation: The forward point launches the tour of tools with the most forceful one.
storyboard.claim: Know your own hammer first, starting with the gas pedal: Red.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson pointing forward like pressing a gas pedal: the forceful tool is next.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the tool in general to the first tool: Red.

storyboard.addedInformation: The target pins Red's aim: results, not people.
storyboard.claim: Red means extroverted and task-oriented, driven by speed and results.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target beside a forceful Bjorn pointing ahead: aim locked on results.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines Red, the gas pedal just promised.

storyboard.addedInformation: The ringing phone stages the setup: out sick with a feverish daughter when Bjorn calls.
storyboard.claim: Meet classic Red Bjorn calling while your daughter has fever for days.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A smartphone beside Bjorn holding his phone: the call about the sick daughter begins.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the Red definition on the phone as Bjorn.

storyboard.addedInformation: The phone stays central: a caring question asked through the device.
storyboard.claim: Bjorn asks how your sick daughter is; you answer she is better.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bjorn on his smartphone asking the question, the caring opener of the call.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the staged call with Bjorn's caring question.

storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face is the flatness: data received, nothing more.
storyboard.claim: Told the fever broke, Bjorn just says Okay.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bjorn flat-faced on the phone: the one-word answer after good news.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers Bjorn's flat reply to the good news.

storyboard.addedInformation: The phone icon is the hang-up itself: connection gone, no pleasantries.
storyboard.claim: Then dial tone: no relief, no love sent, just an abrupt end.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The smartphone with the call ended: Bjorn gone without pleasantries.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts the call dead after the Okay.

storyboard.addedInformation: The sad stare at the dead phone shows the insult without words.
storyboard.claim: If you are not Red, you stare at the screen feeling deeply insulted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped over his smartphone, staring at the dead screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the non-Red aftermath of the hang-up.

storyboard.addedInformation: The angry accusation faces the viewer: judgment replacing the hurt.
storyboard.claim: You feel like a data point and judge him an insensitive jerk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman angrily venting to camera: the verdict on Bjorn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the insult into the jerk verdict.

storyboard.addedInformation: The thinking explainer reframes the call as mechanism, not malice.
storyboard.claim: Strip your projections: see the Red drive behind the call.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Erikson thinking it through: the same call re-examined as wiring.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Steps back from the jerk verdict to re-examine the drive.

storyboard.addedInformation: The even face beside the struck phrase refuses the rude staging.
storyboard.claim: Reds are not actively trying to be rude.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bjorn speaking evenly, no snarl: the rudeness charge struck, not staged.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the jerk verdict: no malice behind the Okay.

storyboard.addedInformation: The target beside the phone shows care expressed as data wanted.
storyboard.claim: Reds run on task completion; Bjorn asked because he wanted the data.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target beside Bjorn on the phone: efficiency aimed at the answer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the caring inside the blunt call.

storyboard.addedInformation: The closed file of notes makes the finished objective visible.
storyboard.claim: Once the fever-broke data arrived, the objective was achieved and filed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bjorn holding a closed file of notes: the case shut the moment data landed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the call the moment its objective lands.

storyboard.addedInformation: The flat face beside the struck politeness shows Red's opposite reading.
storyboard.claim: To a Red, lingering for pleasantries is not polite.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bjorn flatly speaking: the lingering-is-polite rule struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the politeness rule for lingering.

storyboard.addedInformation: The clock is the valued resource itself: time, not abstract speed.
storyboard.claim: Pleasantries waste the one resource Reds value most: time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock beside Bjorn: the time that lingering burns.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what lingering costs: time.

storyboard.addedInformation: The seated boss in the meeting frames the CEO anecdote now starting.
storyboard.claim: Reds measure worth by velocity: enter the Red CEO meeting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart seated at the boardroom table, stern and impatient, the meeting underway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens from Bjorn's call to the CEO who lives by velocity.

storyboard.addedInformation: The forceful point is the slam the rig can draw: debate cut off.
storyboard.claim: Twenty minutes into vendor risks, the CEO slams his hand down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart jabbing his hand down toward the table, cutting the debate short.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Detonates the slow meeting with the table slam.

storyboard.addedInformation: The barking boss is the quote: millions at stake, decide now.
storyboard.claim: He barks the classic Red line: get it together, how hard can it be.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart barking across the table: the order to just decide.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Voices the slam: the bark after the hand.

storyboard.addedInformation: The jabbing point demands motion over paralysis.
storyboard.claim: Pick one and go: any decision beats analytical paralysis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart pointing hard at the team: forward, not more analysis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Presses the bark into the demand: decide and move.

storyboard.addedInformation: The surprised interruption breaks the Red streak to challenge it.
storyboard.claim: Momentum is Red's only state, but the co-host stops to challenge it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman cutting in, surprised: the hold-up before the narcissist charge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Halts the momentum story to question it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The angry finger names the suspicion the CEO and Bjorn provoke.
storyboard.claim: The instinct is not momentum but narcissist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman accusing to camera: the narcissist label voiced.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the counter-reading the interruption held back.

storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer strings make control literal: one man pulling the room.
storyboard.claim: It sounds like an egomaniac tyrant bossing the room to inflate himself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Puppeteer strings over looming Stuart pointing down: control of the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Paints the tyrant picture behind the charge.

storyboard.addedInformation: The barking boss carries the accusation Reds constantly hear.
storyboard.claim: The markers mirror egomania, so Reds are called dictators.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart barking at the table: the dictator accusation made visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the tyrant image into the standing accusation.

storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy in hand is prestige itself: the prize the egomaniac craves.
storyboard.claim: The egomaniac craves power for the sake of prestige.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy clutched by a smirking Everyman: power wanted as a prize.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Splits the lookalikes: the egomaniac wants the prize.

storyboard.addedInformation: Blank indifference beside the struck office shows prestige rejected.
storyboard.claim: A true Red does not care about titles and adoration at all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart impassive, the corner-office prize struck away beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the trophy-clutcher: the Red refuses the prize.

storyboard.addedInformation: The forward point aims at the landscape ahead, not at admirers.
storyboard.claim: Reds want charge not for admiration but for the fastest route.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stuart pointing past the team toward the route ahead: command for pace, not praise.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces admiration with the landscape ahead.
